# Jeremiah 38 — Disagreement Log
**Generated by:** SOPHIA | **Threshold:** <70% word overlap

---

## 38:13 (overlap: 11%)

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | And-they-pulled Jeremiah up with-the-ropes and-lifted-him out-of the-cistern; and-Jeremiah remained in-the-court-of the-guard. |
| LOGOS | So they drew Jeremiah up with ropes and lifted him out of the cistern. And Jeremiah remained in the court of the guard. |
| PNEUMA | So they pulled Jeremiah out of the cistern with the ropes and lifted him out. After that Jeremiah remained in the courtyard of the guard. |

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | And-Ebed-Melech the-Cushite, a-eunuch who [was] in-the-king's house, heard that they-had-put Jeremiah into-the-cistern — and-the-king was-sitting in-the-Gate-of Benjamin — |
| LOGOS | When Ebed-Melech the Ethiopian, a eunuch who was in the king's house, heard that they had put Jeremiah into the cistern — the king was sitting in the Benjamin Gate — |
| PNEUMA | But an Ethiopian official named Ebed-Melech, who served in the royal palace, heard that Jeremiah had been thrown into the cistern. At that time the king was holding court at the Benjamin Gate, |

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

| EMET | And-they-took Jeremiah and-cast-him into-the-cistern-of Malchijah the-king's-son, which [was] in-the-court-of the-guard; and-they-let Jeremiah down with-ropes. And-in-the-cistern [there was] no water, but-only mud, and-Jeremiah sank in-the-mud. |
| LOGOS | So they took Jeremiah and cast him into the cistern of Malchijah, the king's son, which was in the court of the guard, letting Jeremiah down by ropes. And there was no water in the cistern, but only mud, and Jeremiah sank in the mud. |
| PNEUMA | So they took Jeremiah and threw him into the cistern that belonged to Malchijah, a member of the royal family. It was in the courtyard of the guard. They lowered Jeremiah with ropes into the cistern, which had no water but was full of mud. Jeremiah sank deep into the mud. |

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.
